hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier finding 1 (major) was real and is fixed: concurrent mutate.py runs sharing hxcc's build dir corrupted each other's results
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced before the fix: two runs with -o g2coll{job}.exe started 1 s apart; run D's baseline failed with 'LNK1104: cannot open file ...\.obj-g2coll0-69aaf8c973\hxdemo.obj'. Fix: {job} now expands to '<run id>-<index>' (run id = 'mr'+8 hex, per invocation), new {run} and {tmp} (per-job private dir, deleted) placeholders, products in <data dir>/build/hxcc carrying the run id are deleted at the end, default --out-dir carries the run id, and a warning fires for any -o without a unique placeholder regardless of --jobs. After the fix: two concurrent full runs (-o g2conc{job}.exe, 4 jobs each, seed 1) both gave killed 110 / timeout 2 / survived 12 / build-error 0, identical mutant-by-mutant to a solo run, and no g2conc* files remained in the build dir. Regression test test_mutate_concurrent_runs_do_not_collide runs two mutate.py processes at once against a fake hxcc that detects overwritten outputs.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier finding 2 (major) is fixed: waves.py ownership overlap detection handles directories without '/', '//', '/./', trailing '/.', and case variants
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Probe before the fix: all five pairs reported conflict=False. norm_path now canonicalises segments; paths_overlap compares casefolded segment prefixes regardless of trailing '/'; non-canonical spellings warn; case-only conflicts are labelled. test_waves_ownership_overlap_spellings (6 pairs, CLI exit 1) and test_waves_path_canonicalisation pass. 'waves.py validate' on the real tasks.json still prints OK with no warnings.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Minor findings 3-12 are fixed, each with a regression test that fails on the old code
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced first with a probe against the old tools (skeleton gave gen-003/parent gen-002; newline/Arabic-digit/NaN manifests had 0 errors in both engines; string constraints_touched gave 11 errors; $ref self-cycle raised RecursionError; escalate=False with a template saying stop; ADR dates 20261004 and 2026-W40-1 accepted; invariant breaker not tripped by a trailing-newline ADR edit; gen_c mutated #if 0 / #else code, skipped '4 * 1024' at file scope and 'atomic_n * 3'; old generator mutated '+' and '1' inside a t-string under Python 3.14.5; mermaid declared T01_a twice). Fixes: validate_handover --write/--handovers-dir plus numbering that ignores empty or unparsable files and copies the parent's real generation_id, and lineage warnings; check_golden --run (isolated golden suite) with the CI steps switched to it; decisions.yml on labeled/unlabeled; ECMA-262 pattern semantics in both engines ('$' as \Z, ASCII classes), date-time with fullmatch and [0-9], NaN/Infinity rejected, constraints checks only for lists, $ref-cycle SchemaError, RecursionError reported; friction template matches the escalation rule (2 notes), OSError gives exit 2, --task resolves <data dir>/attempts/<id>.jsonl; adr Date must be YYYY-MM-DD before fromisoformat, invariants breaker needs a new or substantively changed ADR citing INVARIANTS.md or a changed INV id; mutate C preprocessor model (three-valued #if/#ifdef/#elif/#else/C23 #elifdef, include guards, #define/#undef through quoted headers, host macro model, -D/-U), initializer-aware file-scope '*', explicit stdatomic type list, sizeof(T *) not a cast, TSTRING tokens skipped, Ctrl-C cancels/kills/cleans up (exit 130), timed-out mutants re-run alone; mermaid index ids with entity escaping. The t-string fix was verified by running the generator under Python 3.14.5 (no pytest there); the corresponding test is skipped on 3.13.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: check_golden --run alone protects the golden suite from code on PYTHONPATH
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: With PYTHONPATH=python, a python/sitecustomize.py calling os._exit(0) ran inside the *outer* 'python check_golden.py' process before the tool started: exit 0, empty output. The tool cannot defend against code that runs before it, so CI runs 'python -E governance/tools/check_golden.py --run' without PYTHONPATH (the tool adds <root>/python itself, after importing pytest). The test now asserts both the hijack and the -E defence.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: pytest with an external -c ini and --rootdir collects only below the root
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: With the temp ini under %TEMP% (8.3 short path) and the repo under the long path, pytest 8.4.2 started collection at a common ancestor and failed on a socket file in %TEMP% ('WinError 1920 ... jb.station.ij.10280.sock'). Fixed with --confcutdir <root> and a resolved ini path; verified with all four combinations.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Patching os.name is a safe way to test the POSIX branch of friction.data_dir on Windows
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Python 3.13 Path() consults os.name at call time: 'cannot instantiate PosixPath on your system'. data_dir now takes an explicit windows= parameter for tests.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Heredoc-fed Python patch scripts in this Bash tool preserve backslashes
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Two patch scripts failed because their double backslashes arrived halved (an escaped newline became a real one). Patches containing backslashes were rewritten as files with the Write tool. Process note for successors, not a product issue.
